unresolved_added: The official task statement is unavailable, so task requirements are reconstructed only from the paper's Summary and internal Requirement references.
Summary claims of 73% and 87% correct rates, tau 0.86, and a named leader are paper-internal results without independent reproduction.
The linear-separability premise for conspirators and non-conspirators is asserted without a diagnostic, margin analysis, or alternative classifier.
Network stability over a long period is assumed even though message time, organizational change, and label timing are not modeled.
The EZ and 83-node networks are assumed to share an information-transmission mechanism without a transportability test.
Behavioral assumptions about conspirators, outsiders, irrelevant topics, leader contacts, and non-conspirator knowledge can encode investigator expectations into features.
The three centrality normalizations and shortest-path conventions are not reconciled with disconnected nodes, direction, ties, or standard alternative definitions.
Known-neighbor and known-conspirator-message features reuse labeled nodes and can leak label proximity into both fitting and evaluation.
Topic 16 is discarded as wrong without a versioned correction log, source reason, denominator effect, or sensitivity rerun.
The paper alternates between gradient ascent and gradient descent language and supplies no code, convergence tolerance, scaling, seed, or coefficient table.
The internal logistic score is called a probability without calibration, uncertainty, class threshold, or cost-sensitive decision rule.
Only 15 labeled nodes are available; leave-one-out variance, label composition, class balance, and fold-specific predictions are not reported.
Regularization is selected on the same leave-one-out process used to report error, without nested model selection or an external test set.
Zero training error with a small labeled set is reported without an overfitting, coefficient-stability, or feature-ablation analysis.
The manager identity choice uses the larger out-degree among duplicate names, a post hoc identity rule that can change the plotted interpretation.
The semantic dictionary is hand-built from known suspicious messages, so vocabulary leakage, lexical ambiguity, annotator disagreement, and drift are unmeasured.
Resource-allocation notation and index direction are ambiguous, and the equations omit tokenization, word counts, repeated terms, normalization, and empty-degree cases.
The error drop from 0.27 to 0.13 follows feature discovery and retraining on the same 15 labels; the enhancement is not nested or independently held out.
The prose says topic 4 is appended even though Table 3 places topics 1,3,4,6,8,9,10,14 at similarity zero, creating an unresolved result-to-action inconsistency.
The O(n) complexity claim excludes expert-dictionary construction, text preprocessing, graph creation, analyst review, memory, and the source's own large-noise bottleneck.
The displayed LeaderRank update multiplies by v_i(t) rather than an explicitly indexed neighbor score; the source notation is retained but not silently repaired.
The suspicious-topic subgraph condition uses unclear set-containment notation and does not define messages with multiple topics or empty intersections.
Every communication edge is reversed under the untested premise that a criminal leader sends commands rather than receives reports or delegates through intermediaries.
Adding a ground node and reversing edges alter topology; convergence, manipulation robustness, and parameter-free behavior are cited rather than reproduced on this graph.
Yao's LeaderRank result is cross-checked with degree and betweenness computed on the same network and a literature heuristic, not an independent leader label.
Kendall tau 0.86 measures rank agreement, while Table 5 and Figure 7 show material probability movement; rank stability is not probability calibration or action stability.
The label-error stress curve assumes independent wrong classifications, gives no simulation protocol or uncertainty interval, and does not test correlated or adversarial errors.
The paper admits feature non-portability and dictionary construction failure at scale; no external network, runtime, privacy, ethics, false-positive cost, or deployment validation is supplied.
